_comment: LRAUV, real xdyn dynamics, drift-only: no Guidance/Control/feedback
loop at all. lrauv.yml's propeller declares an xdyn command key, so
unlike a hull-only vessel it needs some command every step or xdyn
stalls -- static_command_allocation supplies one fixed resting
command forever and never varies it. No gain to tune, no feedback
loop, nothing that can diverge -- structurally the same guarantee as
fremm_drift_only.json, just for a vehicle whose actuator needs an
explicit resting value instead of an absent Allocation task.
propeller(rpm) is 1.5708, NOT 0.0: this vehicle's Kt(J)&Kq(J) curve
(added 5db1e19) computes J = (1-w)*|u-current|/(n*D), and n=0 is a
literal division by zero (J=inf) that xdyn hard-aborts on --
confirmed via the standalone xdyn CLI, rpm 0/2/5/10 all diverge the
same way ('Received x0 = ... but x0 should be within [-0.001,1.5]'),
the sim silently freezes at its last valid state once the real
pipeline's websocket loop hits this (read as 'not moving / not
taking the current' from the outside). The value here is in
RADIANS/SECOND, not RPM, despite the 'rpm' key name --
static_command_allocation passes this dict straight through to
xdyn's runtime command API with no unit conversion, and that API
expects rad/s (confirmed by reading xdyn's own
AbstractWageningen::advance_ratio, `n = commands.at("rpm")/(2*PI)`
-- same finding lrauv_gnc/allocation_task.py's RESOLVED 2026-08-14
note documents for the real Allocation task). A first attempt at
this fix used the literal number 15.0 meaning '15 RPM' and it
silently became 15 rad/s (~143 RPM) once live -- xdyn accepted it
(no crash) but the vehicle accelerated well past the current speed,
confirmed both via the standalone CLI (u climbing past 0.33 m/s and
still rising at t=20s when the raw value is read as rad/s) and via
a real scenario_launch.sh run. 1.5708 rad/s = 15 RPM: the lowest
RPM that keeps J in-domain for this vehicle's drift range (u
decaying from 0.2 toward the current's 0.1 m/s), verified against
the standalone CLI's own YAML `unit: rpm` tag (which DOES convert
correctly) converging to u~0.105 m/s over 60s -- within noise of
the true zero-thrust case (~0.1015 m/s, current speed) confirmed
separately with the propeller block removed entirely. Not
literally resting, but the closest this propeller curve allows
without crashing.
This says nothing about controllability: it never reads Control's
output, only that the vehicle drifts correctly under real
hydrodynamics + current with its propeller near-idle.
